        <section class="content article-content mb-6" itemprop="articleBody">
          <p data-start="485" data-end="815">The Looker connector tools in Optimizely Opal let you query <a href="https://cloud.google.com/looker" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Looker</a> data directly in <a href="/hc/en-us/articles/36343492268813" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Opal Chat</a>, <a href="/hc/en-us/articles/39407442255245" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">agents</a>, and <a href="/hc/en-us/articles/39417564742797" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">workflows</a>. After you add the Looker Opal connector tool and authenticate it in Optimizely Connect Platform (OCP), you can retrieve dashboards, run reports, search content, and use Looker data inside automated workflows.</p><p data-start="817" data-end="869">Complete the following steps to enable Looker connector tools in Opal.</p><h2 id="h_01K86CPG4DW356CY1JZDQ3A2DV">Add the<span lang="EN-US" data-contrast="auto"> Opal Looker Tool</span><span data-ccp-props="{}"> </span>app in OCP<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01K86CPG4DW356CY1JZDQ3A2DV"></a></h2><p>In the OCP <strong>App Directory</strong>, complete the following:</p><ol>
<li data-list-item-id="ec547010a6d6c3f008fab021d6bdcf732">
<p>Click<strong> Opal Looker Tool</strong>.</p>
<figure class="wysiwyg-image"><img style="aspect-ratio: 1860/1012;" src="/hc/article_attachments/41601509890061" width="1860" height="1012" class="img-enlargable"></figure>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e864df95d6302ecc0b99778fad1503167">
<p>Click <strong>Install</strong> <strong>App</strong>.</p>
<figure class="wysiwyg-image"><img style="aspect-ratio: 1848/672;" src="/hc/article_attachments/41601509893517" width="1848" height="672" class="img-enlargable"></figure>
</li>
</ol><p data-start="1085" data-end="1215">Because Looker uses API keys, authentication requires generating an API key pair in Looker and providing those credentials in OCP.</p><h2 id="h_01KB07R8AT3FXM0JPZW5JPZAXG">Generate an API key in Looker<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KB07R8AT3FXM0JPZW5JPZAXG"></a></h2><p data-start="1259" data-end="1298">In Looker, complete the following steps:</p><ol data-start="1300" data-end="1520">
<li data-start="1300" data-end="1364" data-list-item-id="e021677b6ae3f4e3154f4c98d91604216">Go to <strong data-start="1309" data-end="1318">Admin</strong><strong> ></strong> <strong data-start="1321" data-end="1346">Users and Permissions</strong><strong> > </strong><strong data-start="1349" data-end="1361">API Keys</strong>.</li>
<li data-start="1365" data-end="1415" data-list-item-id="e4a287de5cb4454b571cb15b7823256b5">Click <strong data-start="1374" data-end="1389">New API Key</strong> to generate a key pair.</li>
<li data-start="1416" data-end="1520" data-list-item-id="eaac1e47e5577c2882a2b772a27cff5b7">Record the <strong data-start="1430" data-end="1443">Client ID</strong> and <strong data-start="1448" data-end="1458">Secret</strong>.<ul data-start="1465" data-end="1520"><li data-start="1465" data-end="1520" data-list-item-id="e5a0bc874771920c64ec9130260756a2b">Treat the Secret as a password and store it securely.</li></ul>
</li>
</ol><p data-start="1467" data-end="1520">See the <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/api-auth" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Looker API authentication documentation</a> for more information.</p><h2 id="h_01KB07R8AWQ4J42MGBKX1A6VK3">Authenticate the Looker connector tool in OCP<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KB07R8AWQ4J42MGBKX1A6VK3"></a></h2><p data-start="1575" data-end="1649">After you <a href="#h_01KB07R8AT3FXM0JPZW5JPZAXG">generate your Looker API key</a>, authenticate the connector in OCP.</p><ol>
<li data-start="1651" data-end="1722" data-list-item-id="ed00998d4b68aafc309a0c476ede8e94f">Click the <strong data-start="1664" data-end="1684">Opal Looker Tool</strong> connector in the OCP App Directory.</li>
<li data-start="1723" data-end="1755" data-list-item-id="e4834da85095cc3970df1e0d51fbf955d">Go to the <strong data-start="1736" data-end="1748">Settings</strong> tab.</li>
<li data-start="1756" data-end="1857" data-list-item-id="e1de1c41e0907035668701454646466eb">Enter the following in <strong>Looker Authentication </strong>section:<ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-bold" data-start="1815" data-end="1832" data-list-item-id="e4ca163fef5f9728271c75ecc1f8cf39e"><strong data-start="1817" data-end="1830">Looker Client ID</strong></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-bold" data-start="1836" data-end="1857" data-list-item-id="e2bf52693e276019d62820b7fa5565294"><strong data-start="1838" data-end="1855">Looker Client Secret</strong></li>
<li data-start="1836" data-end="1857" data-list-item-id="eeda7eac98dcbc6e1ad6c05ef10a068ec">
<strong data-start="1895" data-end="1918">Looker Instance URL </strong>–  Example: <code data-start="1936" data-end="1969">https://your-company.looker.com</code>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="1972" data-end="1990" data-list-item-id="e624532828f28b57299eae51d17ebc188">
<p>Click <strong data-start="1981" data-end="1989">Save</strong>.</p>

<li data-list-item-id="e8c6f433e920282bf338b04977a76c04e">(Optional) <code>result_format</code> – The format you want the report results in. Options include the following: <ul data-axiom="1.7.1">

<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e4791b8372e0bec6b7fced05275e271aa">
<code data-axiom="1.7.1">csv</code> – Comma-separated values (if you specifically need CSV).</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="ed9d5e52ebc43c4f7850723b8d731894d">
<code data-axiom="1.7.1">txt</code> – Tab-separated text.</li>

</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="ebe1add3e50a35276fcf13d279a93864a">(Optional) <code>apply_formatting</code> – Whether to apply Looker's default formatting (like currency symbols, date formats) to the data. <li class="ck-list-marker-bold" data-list-item-id="e8a812bbd0517e703450e148709fca4f0">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul data-axiom="1.7.1">
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="ef0d5086312e7c315bb1dddf659093fea"><em>Run the Look with ID 123 and give me the results in CSV format.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e284feadf7651763c5e54bbe7dd2f4ed8"><em>Can you execute Look 456 and apply the standard formatting?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e8331e8e1fd8b065176e61a25da840fb5"><em>Get the data from Look 789, but only show me the first 50 rows.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e3cf5f657066c90c4c00a878c05e9fb80"><em>I need the results from Look 1011, formatted as JSON.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>looker_run_query</code> – Executes a Looker query to retrieve data from your data warehouse.</summary><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-bold" data-list-item-id="efe81a553d0166ec15d6561d38d0cd508">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ea07716b98428f4b90031de2899190bc0">Answer specific data questions.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="efb2fc562007ef489ed20dd59311d2624">Explore data dynamically.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ebaf37c2de565f27acd7fd9ef89f75cc7">Build custom reports.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e7a6bc65f44205c84fc23c75e6e24b37a">Get fresh data. </li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-bold" data-list-item-id="e8dbeabe136c2738f041eb0df6cf2d965">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ee8f4b8a89b958c6831ee2549070ee69c">
<code>model</code> – The name of the LookML model you want to query. Use the <code>looker_get_all_models</code> tool from the <a href="#h_01KB06H8D76MKT758BQ5AFWZNT">Retrieve dashboards, Looks, and models</a> section to get a list of available models.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e8cd93718e52b82861b64061a36339a25">
<code>view</code> – The specific "view" or "explore" within the model that contains the data fields you are interested in. Use the <code data-axiom="1.7.1">looker_get_lookml_model_explore</code> tool from the <a href="#h_01KB06H8D76MKT758BQ5AFWZNT">Retrieve dashboards, Looks, and models</a> section with a model name to see available views and their fields.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e0a9be054f7e36930ef08403798fb2af4">
<code>fields</code> – The specific data points (dimensions and measures) you want to see in your report. Provide a comma-separated list of field names, each in the format <code data-axiom="1.7.1">VIEW_NAME.FIELD_NAME</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ed99c47f5bccd1e21d3801f5b234d92d4">(Optional) <code>filters</code> – Criteria to narrow down your data. This is where you specify conditions like date ranges, specific values, or exclusions. This is a JSON string where keys are field names (<code data-axiom="1.7.1">view.field</code>) and values are the filter expressions. <ul data-axiom="1.7.1">
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e6526145c2fe903910aa009f72d1c7329">
<strong data-axiom="1.7.1">Fuzzy matching </strong>– Opal uses a fuzzy match pattern by default (for example, <code data-axiom="1.7.1">%value%</code>) for string filters unless you explicitly ask for an exact match. This helps find partial matches.</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="ef473be1cf961c1756123871b7c16f4d6">
<strong data-axiom="1.7.1">Case sensitivity</strong> – Looker's database is case-sensitive, so it preserves the original case in your filter values.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="edfe5ef783ed3e7d8a710569f44101714">(Optional) <code>sorts</code> – How you want your results ordered.</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e54e5e7d8392d6984671d68919ac7d164">(Optional) <code>limits</code> – The maximum number of rows you want in your final result.</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e30dd622e21f28c2c6bd8ed7976309186">(Optional) <code>result_format</code> – The format you want the query results in. Options include the following: <ul data-axiom="1.7.1">
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e6106ab5cbfd5dbafac3bdd23378e607d">
<code data-axiom="1.7.1">json</code> – Structured JSON data (recommended for most cases, the default).</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="efbedff7d37c8a20664769db327bec16d">
<code data-axiom="1.7.1">csv</code> – Comma-separated values (if you specifically need CSV).</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="ebd2335f3849412a48495b083cb2dcc85">
<code data-axiom="1.7.1">txt</code> – Tab-separated text.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e5c148e6474eab35a213d0496f9c38614">(Optional) <code>apply_formatting</code> – Whether to apply Looker's default formatting to the data values.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-bold" data-list-item-id="eeb731ab8f2d86bd280012806a06c6c8a">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul data-axiom="1.7.1">
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e343808e09d95f1515c069cb87fa55d12">
<em>Show me the </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>orders.id</em></code><em>, </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>orders.created_date</em></code><em>, and </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>orders.total_amount</em></code><em> from the </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>ecommerce</em></code><em> model and </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>orders</em></code><em> view for orders placed </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>this month</em></code><em>.</em>
</li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e1d46e6a43fb9256449e9639b92ccd690">

</li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e6cd86b9a18d17b6bf46862af309e6e26">
<em>I need a list of </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>products.name</em></code><em> and </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>products.category</em></code><em> from the </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>inventory</em></code><em> model and </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>products</em></code><em> view, but only for products where the </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>products.stock_level</em></code><em> is less than 10, and limit the results to 50.</em>
</li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e0da99a3b792ce74227544b6484d87b31">
<em>Find the </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>events.name</em></code><em> and </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>events.count</em></code><em> from the </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>analytics</em></code><em> model and </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>events</em></code><em> view for events that happened </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>yesterday</em></code><em>, and I want an exact match for </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>events.name</em></code><em> being 'page_view'.</em>
</li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e2d0a55285f2a6a3d21f341ae02a694aa">
<em>What are the </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>orders.id</em></code><em>, </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>orders.status</em></code><em>, and </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>users.email</em></code><em> for all orders in the </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>ecommerce</em></code><em> model and </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>orders</em></code><em> view where the </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>orders.status</em></code><em> is 'pending' or 'processing', and the </em><code data-axiom="1.7.1"><em>orders.total_amount</em></code><em> is greater than 50?</em>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>looker_get_query</code> – Retrieves a saved query by ID to retrieve the query definition and metadata.</summary><ul>

<strong>When to use</strong><ul data-axiom="1.7.1">
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e6298b55dcbb3f8e6d603c01ff912f564">

<strong data-axiom="1.7.1">Understand how a query is constructed</strong> – See a query ID's underlying logic without running the query itself.</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e549439418b71a808d3907c221983be94">
<strong data-axiom="1.7.1">Get query metadata</strong> – Retrieve information like when it was created, who owns it, and its unique ID.</li>

<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="efd804665cef09ba2a176c635d40acdc7">
<strong data-axiom="1.7.1">Debug or analyze existing queries</strong> – Understand why a query might be returning certain results or behaving in a particular way.</li>

<li class="ck-list-marker-bold" data-list-item-id="ec858ff8cf4e45f9ce9d84b23dced24c1">

<li data-list-item-id="ed4f81199fe90d79f30e521def4ac9ea3">(Optional) <code>fields</code> – A comma-separated list of specific pieces of information you want to get about the query. <li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e90d7ee73ef307d2c2f17c74ed663ec48">
<code data-axiom="1.7.1">id</code>:– The query's unique ID.</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="edacc0eacfcfe23585a753214277cc9b4">
<code data-axiom="1.7.1">model</code> – The LookML model the query uses.</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="ece56bbcd66a33056135fee322ce90079">

<code data-axiom="1.7.1">fields</code> – The dimensions and measures selected in the query.</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="eb1d95bb4578077ea716ad2110a06c33b">
<code data-axiom="1.7.1">filters</code> – The filters applied to the query.</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e03998e66e9df5240ce9e564bee432775">
<code data-axiom="1.7.1">sorts</code> – How the query results are sorted.</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e5ece56b5d576a6d6871288b156cc4428">
<code data-axiom="1.7.1">limit</code> – Any row limit set for the query.</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e17974718855f25039a992ba8111b119b">
<code data-axiom="1.7.1">created_at</code> – When the query was created.</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e5bc743fabbb8092b47d2453ea7197bed">
<code data-axiom="1.7.1">user_id</code> – The ID of the user who created the query.</li>

</li>

<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="eb8a08d3cd7ffbf1160815f30630de0fb"><em>Can you get me the details of query ID 123?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e5a1d6c3ad46055c00141f153dd8d4812"><em>Show me the fields, filters, and sorts for query 456.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e2db1f6bf3b9b93e46591b17dd33b0b82"><em>What model and view does query 789 use?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e3df02384d40e0f68eefdf06407229c9b"><em>I need to see all the information about query 1011, including who created it and when.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>looker_create_look_render_task</code> – Creates a render task to generate exports (PDF, PNG, CSV, and so on) of a Look.</summary><ul>

<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="eb793429d1b0506009cd85b75c77292aa">
<strong data-axiom="1.7.1">Generate printable reports </strong>– Create PDF versions of your Looks.</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e35ee0805c24f77d0c224d9c373d2ffe8">
<strong data-axiom="1.7.1">Create image thumbnails of visualizations</strong> – Get PNG or JPG images of your Looker charts.</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e161bd096a6d8a7df1d223202fc887170">
<strong data-axiom="1.7.1">Export data for external analysis</strong> – Get data in CSV, XLSX, JSON, or TXT formats.</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="ebb82ce4e0b72f7300ce17d89eec5ba3c">

<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="eafae1875a2f7eada71144ff7748d6fb2">
<strong data-axiom="1.7.1">Create downloadable content for users</strong> – Provide a way for others to download data or reports.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-bold" data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e97ddc47cb8e85087979a39946602693e">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e4cd7ac3385347343fc4f2d9f2fa53a6b">

<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="eebace94f6e467812bdb8ac29d62ddc73">

<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="ee6d7794b53407ef5f89a620087e74491">

<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="ef4de81710808c0e1f9d7c75a418aa185">
<code data-axiom="1.7.1">json</code> – JSON data.</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="ebd9095e933bc638d1ebf4a174a26cd92">
<code data-axiom="1.7.1">txt</code> – Plain text data.</li>
</ul>
</li>

<li data-list-item-id="eb2711bd5924108d3ff5f3b4445cd164d">(Optional) <code>height</code> – The height in pixels for image formats (PNG, JPG).</li>

<li data-list-item-id="e72933539178340f8652745e13c2827d0">(Optional) <code>pdf_paper_size</code> – Sets the paper size for PDF documents. Options include the following:<ul data-axiom="1.7.1">

<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="ec2d6009e0d9be98764c607628fe80583">

<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e5277c2cf933df849e661db96e68f8bbd">

</ul>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-bold" data-list-item-id="e2fac1e5c575e6ddd23c8255b566a3c70">

<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e3bca39262de0b29515b46a5c4e292a72"><em>Generate a PDF of Look ID 123.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e409e4740795830484dfe3e5b13af7347"><em>I need a PNG image of Look 456. Can you make it 1200 pixels wide?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="ed9b9cff458f3fa1e3d851aabf0f910c4"><em>Export the data from Look 789 as an Excel spreadsheet.</em></li>

Looker connector tools – Support Help Center                   

[Skip to main content](#page-container)

The Looker connector tools in Optimizely Opal let you query [Looker](https://cloud.google.com/looker) data directly in [Opal Chat](/hc/en-us/articles/36343492268813), [agents](/hc/en-us/articles/39407442255245), and [workflows](/hc/en-us/articles/39417564742797). After you add the Looker Opal connector tool and authenticate it in Optimizely Connect Platform (OCP), you can retrieve dashboards, run reports, search content, and use Looker data inside automated workflows.

Complete the following steps to enable Looker connector tools in Opal.

## Add the Opal Looker Tool app in OCP[](#h_01K86CPG4DW356CY1JZDQ3A2DV)

In the OCP **App Directory**, complete the following:

1.  Click **Opal Looker Tool**.
    
    ![](/hc/article_attachments/41601509890061)
    
2.  Click **Install** **App**.
    
    ![](/hc/article_attachments/41601509893517)
    

Because Looker uses API keys, authentication requires generating an API key pair in Looker and providing those credentials in OCP.

## Generate an API key in Looker[](#h_01KB07R8AT3FXM0JPZW5JPZAXG)

In Looker, complete the following steps:

1.  Go to **Admin** **>** **Users and Permissions** **>** **API Keys**.
2.  Click **New API Key** to generate a key pair.
3.  Record the **Client ID** and **Secret**.
    *   Treat the Secret as a password and store it securely.

See the [Looker API authentication documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/api-auth) for more information.

## Authenticate the Looker connector tool in OCP[](#h_01KB07R8AWQ4J42MGBKX1A6VK3)

After you [generate your Looker API key](#h_01KB07R8AT3FXM0JPZW5JPZAXG), authenticate the connector in OCP.

1.  Click the **Opal Looker Tool** connector in the OCP App Directory.
2.  Go to the **Settings** tab.
3.  Enter the following in **Looker Authentication** section:
    *   **Looker Client ID**
    *   **Looker Client Secret**
    *   **Looker Instance URL** –  Example: `https://your-company.looker.com`
4.  Click **Save**.
    
    ![](/hc/article_attachments/41607886731277)
    

## Register the Looker connector tool in OCP[](#h_01KB07R8AXHN1T8KA2Q4R6X3DB)

After you [authenticate the Looker Opal app](#h_01KB07R8AWQ4J42MGBKX1A6VK3), complete the following steps in OCP:

1.  Go to **Settings** **>** **Add to Opal**.
2.  Click **Add to Opal** for each Opal instance you want to add the Looker connector tools.
    
    ![](/hc/article_attachments/41601509900429)
    

You can now discover and use the Looker connector tools within Opal.

To remove the connection, click **Remove from Opal**.

## Looker connector tools[](#h_01K848F93CBJAWR0BQN6G7KTRT)

After you add and register the Looker connector tools, you can call the following tools in Opal. Click on a tool's name to expand it and learn more about when to use the tool, required and optional parameters, and example prompts on how to call the tool. If you do not provide a required parameter, Opal prompts you for it.

### Retrieve dashboards, Looks, and models[](#h_01KB06H8D76MKT758BQ5AFWZNT)

`looker_get_all_dashboards` – Retrieves all dashboards from your Looker instance.

*   **When to use**
    *   Browse available dashboards in your Looker instance.
    *   Get metadata about dashboards, such as their titles, descriptions, and creators.
    *   Filter dashboards by specific folders or their deletion status.
    *   Understand the overall structure and organization of dashboards within your Looker instance.
    *   Audit dashboard usage and organization.
*   **Parameters**
    *   (Optional) `deleted` – Lets you include dashboards that were soft-deleted (moved to trash). Set to `true` to see deleted dashboards or `false` (default) to see only active ones.
    *   (Optional) `fields` – Specifies which pieces of information you want to retrieve for each dashboard. This can help keep the results clean and focused. Provide a comma-separated list of fields. If you leave it empty, Opal returns a default set of common fields. Useful fields include the following:
        *   `id`
        *   `title`
        *   `description`
        *   `dashboard_filters`
        *   `folder`
        *   `user_id`
        *   `created_at`
        *   `updated_at`
    *   (Optional) `folder_id` – Filters the list to only show dashboards located within a specific folder.
    *   (Optional) `limit` – Sets the maximum number of dashboards to return. Useful for getting a quick sample or for pagination.
    *   (Optional) `offset` – Works with `limit` for pagination. It tells the tool how many dashboards to skip from the beginning of the list.
    *   (Optional) `sorts` – Determines the order in which the dashboards are listed. Provide a comma-separated list of fields to sort by
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _List all the dashboards in Looker._
    *   _Show me the titles and descriptions of all dashboards._
    *   _Can you get me the first 10 dashboards, sorted by their creation date in descending order?_
    *   _I need to see all dashboards, including any deleted ones._
    *   _Find all dashboards and tell me who created them and when they were last updated._

`looker_get_dashboard` – Retrieves detailed information about a dashboard by ID.

*   **When to use**
    *   Get all the detailed information about a single, specific Looker dashboard.
    *   Understand the structure and components of a dashboard, including its tiles, filters, and underlying queries.
    *   Retrieve metadata like the dashboard's title, description, creation date, and last update.
    *   Access the configuration details of a dashboard, perhaps to replicate it or understand how it is built.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `dashboard_id` – Identifies the specific dashboard you are interested in with a unique number.
    *   (Optional) `fields` – Lets you choose which specific pieces of information you want to see about the dashboard. Provide a comma-separated list of the fields you want. Useful fields include the following:
        *   `id`
        *   `title`
        *   `description`
        *   `dashboard_elements` – For tiles and components.
        *   `dashboard_filters` – For filters.
        *   `folder` – For its location.
        *   `user_id` – For who created it.
        *   `created_at` 
        *   `updated_at`
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Tell me everything about dashboard ID 123._
    *   _Can you get the details for dashboard 456, but only show me its title, description, and filters?_
    *   _What are the dashboard elements and queries associated with dashboard 789?_
    *   _I need to see the full configuration for dashboard 101. What information can you provide?_
    *   _Show me the title, creation date, and last updated date for dashboard 2020 dashboard 2022 for dashboard 202._

`looker_get_all_looks` – Retrieves all saved Looks in your instance.

*   **When to use**
    *   Get a list of all saved reports (called Looks) in your Looker instance.
    *   Discover what reports are available that might answer your business questions.
    *   Find predefined dashboards and analyses.
    *   Get quick insights from reports that have already been built.
*   **Parameters**
    *   (Optional) `limit` – How many Looks are returned in a single request. Useful if you only want to see a few examples or if you're dealing with a very large number of Looks.
    *   (Optional) `offset` – Used for pagination, meaning if there are many Looks, you can ask for them in chunks. This tells the tool to skip a certain number of Looks from the beginning of the list.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _List all the saved Looks in Looker._
    *   _Show me the first 25 Looks available._
    *   _Can you get me all the Looks, but start after the first 100?_
    *   _What reports are available in Looker?_
    *   _I need to see a list of all existing analyses that list all the looks._

`looker_get_all_models` – Retrieves all available LookML models. Models are top-level containers that define data connections and explores. 

*   **When to use**
    *   Get a list of all the LookML models available in your Looker instance.
    *   Understand the structure of your data and how it is organized.
    *   Discover what data sources are connected and available for querying.
    *   Find the right model to use when you plan to build new queries or reports.
*   **Parameters**
    *   (Optional) `limit` – Lets you control the maximum number of LookML models that are returned in the list.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _List all the LookML models available in Looker._
    *   _Show me all the data models._
    *   _Can you give me a list of all models, but only show the first 5?_
    *   _What are the different data models we have in Looker?_

`looker_get_lookml_model_explore` – Retrieves metadata for an explore within a LookML model. An explore defines the data structure and relationships available for querying. 

*   **When to use**
    *   Building dynamic query interfaces.
    *   Understanding data relationships.
    *   Validating field names before running queries.
    *   Creating intelligent query builders.
    *   Discovering available fields for queries.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `explore_name` – Name of the explore within the model. 
    *   `lookml_model` – Name of the LookML model containing the explore.
    *   (Optional) `fields` – Comma-separated list of fields to include in the response. Controls which metadata is returned. Useful for performance optimization or when you only need specific information. Common useful fields include the following:
        *   `dimensions`
        *   `measures`
        *   `dimension_groups`
        *   `joins`
        *   `sql_table_name`
        *   `description`
        *   `hidden`
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Tell me about the 'orders' explore in the 'ecommerce' model._
    *   _What dimensions and measures are available in the 'users' explore of the 'customer\_analytics' model?_
    *   _Can you show me the joins defined in the 'events' explore within the 'web\_analytics' model?_
    *   _I need to see all the metadata for the 'products' explore in the 'inventory' model._
    *   _What are the available fields for the 'sales\_facts' explore in the 'sales' model, focusing on dimensions and measures?_

### Run reports and queries[](#h_01KB06HH4A791AQQXN762KWMD0)

`looker_run_look` – Executes a saved Look (report) and returns data results.

*   **When to use**
    *   Run existing reports to get current data.
    *   Access predefined analysis and dashboards.
    *   Get formatted results from saved queries.
    *   Answer questions using previously built reports.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `look_id` – The unique number that identifies a specific saved report (Look) in Looker. You can use the `looker_get_all_looks` from the [Retrieve dashboards, Looks, and models](#h_01KB06H8D76MKT758BQ5AFWZNT) section to find the available Look IDs.
    *   (Optional) `result_format` – The format you want the report results in. Options include the following: 
        *   `json` – Structured JSON data (recommended for most cases, the default).
        *   `csv` – Comma-separated values (if you specifically need CSV).
        *   `txt` – Tab-separated text.
    *   (Optional) `apply_formatting` – Whether to apply Looker's default formatting (like currency symbols, date formats) to the data. Set to `true` if you want the data to look nice for display (this is generally recommended). Set to `false` if you need the raw data for further processing.
    *   (Optional) `limit` – The maximum number of rows you want to see in the results.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Run the Look with ID 123 and give me the results in CSV format._
    *   _Can you execute Look 456 and apply the standard formatting?_
    *   _Get the data from Look 789, but only show me the first 50 rows._
    *   _I need the results from Look 1011, formatted as JSON._

`looker_run_query` – Executes a Looker query to retrieve data from your data warehouse.

*   **When to use**
    *   Answer specific data questions.
    *   Explore data dynamically.
    *   Build custom reports.
    *   Get fresh data. 
*   **Parameters**
    *   `model` – The name of the LookML model you want to query. Use the `looker_get_all_models` tool from the [Retrieve dashboards, Looks, and models](#h_01KB06H8D76MKT758BQ5AFWZNT) section to get a list of available models.
    *   `view` – The specific "view" or "explore" within the model that contains the data fields you are interested in. Use the `looker_get_lookml_model_explore` tool from the [Retrieve dashboards, Looks, and models](#h_01KB06H8D76MKT758BQ5AFWZNT) section with a model name to see available views and their fields.
    *   `fields` – The specific data points (dimensions and measures) you want to see in your report. Provide a comma-separated list of field names, each in the format `VIEW_NAME.FIELD_NAME`.
    *   (Optional) `filters` – Criteria to narrow down your data. This is where you specify conditions like date ranges, specific values, or exclusions. This is a JSON string where keys are field names (`view.field`) and values are the filter expressions. 
        *   **Fuzzy matching** – Opal uses a fuzzy match pattern by default (for example, `%value%`) for string filters unless you explicitly ask for an exact match. This helps find partial matches.
        *   **Case sensitivity** – Looker's database is case-sensitive, so it preserves the original case in your filter values.
    *   (Optional) `sorts` – How you want your results ordered.
    *   (Optional) `limits` – The maximum number of rows you want in your final result.
    *   (Optional) `result_format` – The format you want the query results in. Options include the following: 
        *   `json` – Structured JSON data (recommended for most cases, the default).
        *   `csv` – Comma-separated values (if you specifically need CSV).
        *   `txt` – Tab-separated text.
    *   (Optional) `apply_formatting` – Whether to apply Looker's default formatting to the data values.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Show me the_ `_orders.id_`_,_ `_orders.created_date_`_, and_ `_orders.total_amount_` _from the_ `_ecommerce_` _model and_ `_orders_` _view for orders placed_ `_this month_`_._
    *   _Can you get me the_ `_users.email_` _and_ `_users.country_` _from the_ `_users_` _view in the_ `_marketing_` _model, but only for users in 'United States' or 'Canada', and sort them by_ `_users.email_` _alphabetically?_
    *   _I need a list of_ `_products.name_` _and_ `_products.category_` _from the_ `_inventory_` _model and_ `_products_` _view, but only for products where the_ `_products.stock_level_` _is less than 10, and limit the results to 50._
    *   _Find the_ `_events.name_` _and_ `_events.count_` _from the_ `_analytics_` _model and_ `_events_` _view for events that happened_ `_yesterday_`_, and I want an exact match for_ `_events.name_` _being 'page\_view'._
    *   _What are the_ `_orders.id_`_,_ `_orders.status_`_, and_ `_users.email_` _for all orders in the_ `_ecommerce_` _model and_ `_orders_` _view where the_ `_orders.status_` _is 'pending' or 'processing', and the_ `_orders.total_amount_` _is greater than 50?_

`looker_get_query` – Retrieves a saved query by ID to retrieve the query definition and metadata.

*   **When to use**
    *   **Inspect existing query definitions** – Understand how a specific query is built, including its fields, filters, and sorting.
    *   **Understand how a query is constructed** – See a query ID's underlying logic without running the query itself.
    *   **Get query metadata** – Retrieve information like when it was created, who owns it, and its unique ID.
    *   **Retrieve query configuration for modification** – See a query's current state if you are planning to make changes to an existing query.
    *   **Debug or analyze existing queries** – Understand why a query might be returning certain results or behaving in a particular way.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `query_id` – The unique numerical identifier for the saved query you want to retrieve. You can find query IDs in Looker URLs when you are viewing a saved query.
    *   (Optional) `fields` – A comma-separated list of specific pieces of information you want to get about the query. This helps you get only what you need and can make the response faster. Common useful fields include the following:
        *   `id`:– The query's unique ID.
        *   `model` – The LookML model the query uses.
        *   `view` – The view or explore within the model.
        *   `fields` – The dimensions and measures selected in the query.
        *   `filters` – The filters applied to the query.
        *   `sorts` – How the query results are sorted.
        *   `limit` – Any row limit set for the query.
        *   `created_at` – When the query was created.
        *   `user_id` – The ID of the user who created the query.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Can you get me the details of query ID 123?_
    *   _Show me the fields, filters, and sorts for query 456._
    *   _What model and view does query 789 use?_
    *   _I need to see all the information about query 1011, including who created it and when._

`looker_create_look_render_task` – Creates a render task to generate exports (PDF, PNG, CSV, and so on) of a Look.

*   **When to use**
    *   **Generate printable reports** – Create PDF versions of your Looks.
    *   **Create image thumbnails of visualizations** – Get PNG or JPG images of your Looker charts.
    *   **Export data for external analysis** – Get data in CSV, XLSX, JSON, or TXT formats.
    *   **Schedule automated report generation** – Regularly produce reports in a specific format.
    *   **Create downloadable content for users** – Provide a way for others to download data or reports.
